<td valign="top" style="width:4.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(2</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 1, 2018, the Company adopted 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (&#8220;ASU 2014-09&#8221;). ASU 2014-09 implements a common revenue standard that clarifies the principles for recognizing revenue. The core principle of ASU 2014-09 is that an entity should recognize revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services. To achieve that core principle, an entity should apply the following steps: (i) identify the contract(s) with a customer, (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) determine the transaction price, (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">144</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:6.61%;">&#160;</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CENTERSTATE BANK CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Dollar amounts in thousands, except per share data)</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December 31, 2018, 2017 and 2016</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000662_dcnt_351b5290-1676-44e7-967a-7b67cf0bbec1" continuedAt="F_000662_dcnt_d69d4a1c-807a-4ecc-ba5d-014431331189">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The<span style="color:#252525;"> </span>Company concluded that there is no change to&#160;the timing and pattern of revenue recognition for its current revenue streams in scope of Topic&#160;606 or&#160;the presentation of revenue as gross versus net. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003361" name="us-gaap:RetainedEarningsAccumulatedDeficit" contextRef="C_0001102266_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member_us-gaapInitialApplicationPeriodCumulativeEffectTransitionAxis_us-gaapDifferenceBetweenRevenueGuidanceInEffectBeforeAndAfterTopic606Member_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">No</ix:nonFraction> adjustment to retained earnings was required on the adoption date.&#160;&#160;Because there is no change to the timing and pattern of revenue recognition, there are no material changes to the Company&#8217;s processes and internal controls.&#160;&#160;Expanded disclosures including disaggregation of revenues and descriptions of performance obligations required by ASU 2014-09 are included below. The Company adopted ASU 2014-09 in the first quarter of 2018 under the modified retrospective approach, and management determined during the assessment of the Company&#8217;s revenue streams that the adoption of ASU 2014-09 did not impact the Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There are two reasons ASU 2014-09 did not have an impact to the Company.&#160;&#160;First, the majority of revenues are interest earned and gain on sales of loans, investment securities and other financial instruments, all of which are unaffected as they are outside the scope of ASU 2014-09.&#160;&#160;Secondly, the Company&#8217;s non-interest income revenue streams such as service charges on deposits, treasury management fees, wealth advisory fees, fixed income sales, and correspondent bank fees, are all within the scope of ASU 2014-09.&#160;&#160;However, ASC Topic 606 focuses on revenues from contracts earned over time, but all of these in-scope noninterest income revenue streams are governed by agreements that do not have an enforceable, contractual term.&#160;&#160;Given the cancellable-at-will structure, ASC Topic 606 views these contracts as agreements-at-will without a defined term, the revenues of which are immediately recognized.&#160;&#160;The revenue recognition timing is identical compared to previous revenue recognition standards.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All of the Company&#8217;s revenue from contracts with customers in the scope of ASC 606 is recognized within Non-Interest Income.&#160;&#160;ASU 2014-09 requires disclosure of sufficient information to understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with customers.&#160;&#160;A description of the Company&#8217;s revenue streams accounted for under ASC 606 as well as an explanation of why they are not impacted are as follows:&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Revenues by Operating Segment/Line of Business</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Correspondent Banking Capital Markets Revenue - Fixed Income Sales</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The company earns commission revenues from the sale of fixed income securities to institutional investors.&#160;&#160;These revenues are earned and collected at each individual sale, and the sale is the sole performance obligation.&#160;&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_003362" name="us-gaap:RevenuePerformanceObligationDescriptionOfGoodOrService" contextRef="C_0001102266_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member_us-gaapInitialApplicationPeriodCumulativeEffectTransitionAxis_us-gaapDifferenceBetweenRevenueGuidanceInEffectBeforeAndAfterTopic606Member_20180101_20181231">There are no minimum orders or future performance obligations or deferred recognition requirements.</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Other Correspondent Banking Related Revenue</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The company earns revenues from a variety of services to other financial institutions including but not limited to correspondent banking, cash and clearing, safekeeping, wire transfers, international services, bond accounting, and others.&#160;&#160;Fixed income sales are discussed separately.&#160;&#160;While there is a significant variety of a la carte services, all (except fixed income sales) are either billed as incurred or are subject to monthly billing, at which point the performance obligation have been fulfilled.&#160;&#160;Even though a Correspondent agreement may provide for services over an indefinite period of time, the customer is free to end the agreement at will without penalty.&#160;&#160;This structure is viewed as an at-will agreement under ASC 606, the revenues of which are recognized immediately.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Service Charges on Deposit Accounts</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company earns fees from its deposit customers for transaction-based, account maintenance, and overdraft services.&#160;&#160;Transaction-based fees, which include but are not limited to: services such as ATM use fees, stop payment charges, statement rendering, ACH fees, are recognized at the time the transaction is executed as that is the point in time the Company fulfills the customer&#8217;s request.&#160;&#160;Maintenance fees, which relate primarily to monthly maintenance, are earned over the course of a month, representing the period over which the Company satisfies the performance obligation.&#160;&#160;Overdraft fees are recognized at the point in time that the overdraft occurs.&#160;&#160;Service charges on deposits are withdrawn from the customer&#8217;s account balance. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Wealth Management Related Revenue - Treasury Management </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company earns fees for Treasury Management products and services which include but are not limited to online cash management, remote deposit capture, positive pay, and lockboxes.&#160;&#160;Similar to the above service charges on deposit accounts above, these fees are also recognized at either the time the transaction or at the end of the month in the case where service obligations are provided over the course of each month.&#160;&#160;Even though a customer&#8217;s Treasury Management agreement may </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">145</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:6.61%;">&#160;</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CENTERSTATE BANK CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Dollar amounts in thousands, except per share data)</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December 31, 2018, 2017 and 2016</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000662_dcnt_d69d4a1c-807a-4ecc-ba5d-014431331189" continuedAt="F_000662_dcnt_d1d49b8d-718e-4a3c-8143-69aafcbfbfed">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">provide for services over an indefinite period of time, the customer is free to end the agreement at will without penalty.&#160;&#160;This structure is viewed as an at-will agreement under ASC 606, the revenues of which are recognized immediately.&#160;&#160;</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;"><br /></span></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">146</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;text-indent:6.61%;">&#160;</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CENTERSTATE BANK CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Dollar amounts in thousands, except per share data)</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December 31, 2018, 2017 and 2016</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000662_dcnt_d1d49b8d-718e-4a3c-8143-69aafcbfbfed">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Wealth Management Related Revenue - Wealth Management &#38; Advisory</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has contracted with a third party to provide wealth management and investment brokerage services on behalf of the Company.&#160;&#160;All fees earned by the Company from Wealth Management and Advisory activities are in the form of a revenue sharing agreement.&#160;&#160;The Company acts as agent in this agreement, and as such, ASC 606 deems the third party to be the customer of the Company as opposed to those individual and entities receiving the wealth advisory services.&#160;&#160;The agreed-upon portion of revenues generated by the third party for services provided other entities and individuals are owed and remitted to the Company at the end of each month, at which time all performance obligations of the Company are fulfilled.&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Wealth Management Related Revenue - Trust</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company sold its Trust Department in December 2017.&#160;&#160;While there would have been ASC Topic 606 revenue recognition timing implications, the sale prior to December 31, 2017 removed these revenues from consideration.&#160;&#160;Trust revenues are displayed for prior periods only.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Debit, Prepaid, ATM and Merchant Card Related Fees - Prepaid Cards</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company earns revenues from prepaid card interchange fees and maintenance fees. Interchange fees from cardholder transactions represent a portion of the underlying transaction value and are recognized daily, concurrently with the transaction processing services to the cardholder.&#160;&#160;Similar to fees from deposits accounts, maintenance fees are earned over the performance obligation period, after which all obligations have been fulfilled.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Debit, Prepaid, ATM and Merchant Card Related Fees - Credit Cards</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company earns revenues from a revenue sharing agreement with a third party who provides credit card services for Company customers.&#160;&#160;Similar to the Wealth Management and Advisory revenue sharing agreement discussed above, the Company is the agent and the third party is the customer.&#160;&#160;The revenue sharing agreement calculates fees owed to the Company based on interchange and application amounts and levels.&#160;&#160;These share of fees are remitted to the Company each month, at which time the performance obligation is fulfilled.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Debit, Prepaid, ATM and Merchant Card Related Fees - Debit Card Interchange Income</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company earns interchange fees from debit cardholder transactions through the MasterCard payment network.&#160; Interchange fees form cardholder transactions represent a percentage of the underlying transaction value and are recognized daily, concurrently with the transaction processing services provided to the cardholder.&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Gains/Losses on Sales of Repossessed Real Estate (&#8220;OREO&#8221;)</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company records a gain or loss from the sale of OREO when control of the property transfers to the buyer, which generally occurs at the time of an executed deed.&#160;&#160;There are no ASC 606 implications unless the Company finances the sale of OREO.&#160;&#160;There are no instances of the Company financing the sale of one of its OREO properties as of September 30, 2018.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Contract Balances</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:5.02%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Contract Balances disclosure requirement is not relevant, as <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003363" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" contextRef="C_0001102266_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201409Member_us-gaapInitialApplicationPeriodCumulativeEffectTransitionAxis_us-gaapDifferenceBetweenRevenueGuidanceInEffectBeforeAndAfterTopic606Member_20180101_20181231" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> revenues are earned over time that would require the monitoring of contract balances.&#160;&#160;The Performance Obligations disclosure requirements call for a description of when performance obligations are satisfied, significant payment terms, nature of goods or services promised, and obligations for returns, refunds, and warranties.&#160;&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.96%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.5%;text-indent:-4.5%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000664" name="csfl:CapitalRaiseTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001102266_20180101_20181231" escape="true">
